title: [Documentation]: Emphasise platform differences still exist with cross-platform support
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Referring to Electron as cross-platform may cause developers to overlook how, even though one JavaScript codebase works for Windows, macOS, and Linux, performance characteristics aren't always the same for all platforms.

I filed an issue to address this for one case earlier:
- `electron/electron#49727`

There, the issue was the `app.getApplicationNameForProtocol` API performing much worse on Linux, as compared to Windows and macOS. The performance disparity was caught as I was testing the application on Linux, in addition to the main developer testing on macOS and Windows.

While the API documentation states **platform availability**, such as an API only being available on macOS, it generally doesn't include whether **performance** might differ across platforms that are supported.

I believe this could mislead developers into thinking an Electron application performs the same across all platforms, and, as a result, overlook any platform specific issues that may come up.

### Proposed Solution

Add a section in [`Docs > Best Practices > Performance`](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/tutorial/performance) that emphasises the possibility for issues to only exist on one platform, even though Electron is a cross-platform framework.

I was thinking a section like:
> ## Platform Differences
> While Electron is a cross-platform framework, there may still be differences between platforms. An API, although it may support Windows, macOS, and Linux, is not guaranteed to **perform** the same across them.
>
> During development, be aware of the possibility that the performance of an Electron application running on your local device may not necessarily be identical performance-wise to the same application running on another platform. 

### Alternatives Considered

These performance differences could also be documented for each API.

I imagine this idea wouldn't be mutually exclusive with the first one.

### Additional Information

I'm making this issue primarily to get any others' thoughts on this, as I reckon this is a pretty big topic.

Happy to have a discussion 🙂
